Menus

posts.title: The Tuesday crates
posts.excerpt: Polder Vegetable Co-op unloads crates of root vegetables at the back door. The short menu starts from that Tuesday delivery.
posts.content:
Every Tuesday morning Polder Vegetable Co-op unloads crates of root vegetables at the back door of Havenstraat 41. Elena Vasquez checks them on the bench before service and writes the week's menu around what arrived.

The delivery is the reason the menu is short. Lunch runs Tuesday to Friday, from 11:30 to 14:30, and dinner Tuesday to Saturday, so the same crates feed both. Fish follows on Wednesday and Friday from Harbour Day Boats.

Two courses at lunch are €26 and three are €32. A vegetarian version of every menu is the same price.

posts.title: Bread at six
posts.excerpt: Jonas Berg shapes loaves on a floured bench at dawn. The flour is stone-milled and arrives weekly from Molen Ten Wind.
posts.content:
Jonas Berg starts at six, when the room is still empty. He shapes the loaves by hand on a floured bench and leaves them to prove while the kitchen wakes up.

The flour is stone-milled and arrives weekly from Molen Ten Wind. The bread goes to the tables at lunch and dinner, and the sourdough is torn, not sliced.

Counter seats are the best place to watch the baking and the plating. Eight seats sit along the pass, and walk-ins may ask for a free one.

posts.title: Pouring by the glass
posts.excerpt: Priya Raman pours white wine by the glass. The four-glass pairing with the dinner menu is €38.
posts.content:
Priya Raman looks after wine and drinks. The by-the-glass list names the grape and the region and nothing more, so the conversation happens at the table.

The wine pairing is four glasses with the dinner menu and costs €38. Her list also holds house-made non-alcoholic drinks, served with each course on request.

The dinner menu is €58 for four courses. The kitchen tasting is six courses for €78.

posts.title: A long table for twelve
posts.excerpt: The private room holds twelve guests around one oak table. Groups of seven to twelve book it through Mateo Rossi.
posts.content:
The private room seats twelve guests around a single long oak table, with a minimum of eight. Daylight comes from the window and the candles stay unlit until the evening.

Mateo Rossi handles reservations and private dining. The dinner menu is €58 per guest and the kitchen tasting is €78; the wine pairing is €38.

Enquire by email at table@shokutaku.example. There is no deposit, and we ask for cancellations at least 24 hours ahead.
